item.title: Add a unique tie-breaker to default cursor ordering centrally
item.description: Fixing non-unique default ordering once in the shared helper (sort_queryset_by_default) covers every default-ordered connection instead of patching each resolver.
item.content: When cursor pagination derives cursors from non-unique ordering fields, append a unique non-nullable field (pk) to the ordering if no primary key is already present. Do it in the single function all default-ordered connections route through, so the fix applies globally and only makes ties deterministic without reordering distinct keys.

item.title: Test pagination by walking multiple pages over tied rows
item.description: Regression tests for cursor pagination must fetch several consecutive pages and assert cursor advancement, not just a single page.
item.content: Create rows that tie on every ordering field (e.g. bulk_create with same sort_order/sku or same created_at), then fetch page 1, page 2, page 3 using each endCursor and assert exact expected IDs per page plus hasNextPage transitions. This catches both the 'same page repeated' and 'group skipped' failure modes that single-page tests miss.

item.title: Flag backward-compatibility impact of cursor format changes
item.description: Changing cursor components invalidates previously issued cursors; reviewers will question the blast radius, so address it explicitly.
item.content: When a fix alters cursor encoding, note in the description that old cursors will be rejected and clients must restart pagination, and confirm that is acceptable. Reviewers may approve the code but still raise this concern, so proactively documenting the trade-off avoids a rejected first attempt.

item.title: Port upstream PRs faithfully, not minimally
item.description: When the task is a port of a specific upstream PR, the reviewer rejects a stripped-down version that omits parts of the original change.
item.content: Fetch and mirror the upstream PR's full scope (settings, schema fields, error codes, docs/ADR, changelog) rather than implementing only the core behavior. A first attempt was rejected as 'Unnecessary' because it deviated from the referenced PR; the accepted version reproduced the upstream design including an ADR and CHANGELOG entry.

item.title: Document accepted risks in an ADR for security features
item.description: Security/traffic-control features in Saleor expect an ADR describing deliberate trade-offs alongside the code.
item.content: When adding a setting that restricts API access, add a docs/adr entry listing accepted risks (cache staleness, replica lag, where the check runs) and a CHANGELOG line under GraphQL API. This matches the accepted final diff and signals the design was considered.

item.title: Never assert through process-global caches in tests
item.description: Caches like Site.objects.get_current() survive across tests, so assertions relying on cache state are order-dependent.
item.content: To verify a write, read the row back with refresh_from_db(fields=(...)) instead of a cached accessor; to count queries, warm the cache first or call clear_cache() explicitly. Also resolve the current site via Site.objects.get_current()/get_site_promise rather than settings.SITE_ID, and key per-site data by the resolved site.

item.title: Autouse fixtures must recreate migration-seeded rows
item.description: Making a fixture autouse that reads a migration-seeded row breaks under transactional test teardown, which truncates all tables and wipes the seeded data.
item.content: When a fixture depends on a row created by a data migration (e.g. a default CustomerType), use get_or_create keyed on the unique flag rather than .get(), and make it autouse only if it self-heals. Transactional tests (django_db(transaction=True)) flush all tables on teardown, so any migration-seeded row is gone for later runs with --reuse-db.

item.title: Centralize default-row creation in a helper
item.description: Extract a get_or_create helper for the default row and reuse it from fixtures, test-user factories, and production code paths.
item.content: Define a single get_or_create_default_<X>() helper and call it from the autouse fixture, from dangerously_create_test_user (only when customer_type isn't explicitly passed), and from random-data generators. This keeps every non-API creation path consistent and avoids duplicating the fallback logic.

item.title: Update tests that assumed the old default behavior
item.description: When a factory starts assigning a default value, tests asserting that field is None must explicitly clear it first.
item.content: After making dangerously_create_test_user assign a default customer_type, tests like test_assign_default_customer_type_task_backfills_users_without_type must use User.objects.filter(...).update(customer_type=None) to set up the precondition, and tests checking existing assignments must explicitly null the other users. Audit all tests relying on the previous implicit None.

item.title: Lock attribute values before deleting them
item.description: Deleting AttributeValue rows without a row lock risks concurrent modification, and reviewers expect consistency with existing deletion paths.
item.content: When deleting AttributeValue rows, wrap the operation in transaction.atomic() and select the target IDs via attribute_value_qs_select_for_update() before calling delete(). ProductDelete, PageBulkDelete, and attributeDelete all do this, so any new deletion path should follow the same pattern.

item.title: Delete per-user attribute values before the user row
item.description: Unique-value AttributeValues are only discoverable through AssignedUserAttributeValue, which the user FK cascade removes.
item.content: To clean up user-owned attribute values, query AssignedUserAttributeValue for the user PKs and delete the matching AttributeValue rows inside the same atomic block, before queryset.delete()/user.delete(). After the user is deleted the assignments are gone and the values become unreachable orphans.

item.title: Scope cleanup to unique-value input types only
item.description: Selectable input types (dropdown, multiselect, swatch) share AttributeValue rows across users, so deleting them would destroy shared choices.
item.content: Filter the AttributeValue deletion by Attribute.input_type__in=AttributeInputType.TYPES_WITH_UNIQUE_VALUES (plain text, rich text, file, reference, numeric, date, datetime). Only those values are created per user and may contain PII; selectable values must survive with just their assignments cascaded away.

item.title: Fail closed on unmapped enum keys in permission maps
item.description: When resolving permissions from a type-to-permission map, an unmapped type must be rejected explicitly rather than raising KeyError or silently passing.
item.content: Before looking up each type in a permission map, check that the set of encountered types is a subset of the map's keys; if not, raise PermissionDenied with all mapped permissions (or emit a row error). This keeps the check fail-closed and avoids 500s when new types are added later.

item.title: Apply the same fix to every duplicated lookup site
item.description: Reviewers flagged the same unsafe map lookup in multiple files (bulk_mutations and attribute_bulk_update), so fix all occurrences together.
item.content: When a permission-resolution helper or pattern is introduced, grep for all call sites of the same lookup and update them consistently; leaving one copy unfixed reintroduces the vulnerability.

item.title: Check concrete permissions after resolving object types
item.description: For mutations whose required permission depends on the target object's type, drop the static Meta.permissions and check permissions inside perform_mutation after fetching types.
item.content: Use a coarse 'any of the relevant permissions' check first, then resolve the actual types from the DB (values_list('type').distinct()) and enforce the per-type permission, requiring all permissions for mixed batches.

item.title: Verify permission claims against actual mutation code
item.description: When documenting permission changes, confirm each mutation's previously required permission by reading the code rather than assuming.
item.content: The first attempt was rejected because a reviewer corrected the stated previous permission for `attributeValueCreate` (it was `MANAGE_PRODUCTS`, not what was written). Before writing changelog entries that enumerate per-mutation permission changes, grep each mutation's `permissions`/`check_permissions` to confirm the exact prior value.

item.title: Use get_global_id_or_error for mutation ID parsing
item.description: Replacing manual `from_global_id_or_error` unpacking with `cls.get_global_id_or_error(object_id, only_type=...)` yields proper GraphQL errors instead of top-level exceptions.
item.content: In Saleor mutations, `cls.get_global_id_or_error(object_id, only_type=Model)` returns the pk and raises a GraphQL error attached to the `id` field with code `GRAPHQL_ERROR` and message `Invalid ID: <id>. Expected: <Type>.`, whereas raw `from_global_id_or_error` unpacking can surface malformed IDs as unhandled errors. Prefer the class helper and add a test asserting the error appears in `data.<mutation>.errors`.

item.title: Document permission changes with upgrade guidance
item.description: Changelog entries for permission changes should list affected mutations, old vs new permissions, and a migration note for staff/apps.
item.content: Structure the entry as: summary of the new rule, a bullet list of each affected mutation with its previous permission and the new per-type requirement, notes on bulk mutations requiring both permissions when targeting mixed types, and a 'To upgrade' sentence telling users which permissions to grant. This matches reviewer expectations and makes the breaking change actionable.

item.title: Compare IDs as strings when diffing GraphQL input pks against DB pks
item.description: GraphQL global IDs decode to string pks while DB values_list returns ints, so set differences silently report every input as missing.
item.content: When checking existence of decoded global IDs against DB rows, normalize both sides to the same type (e.g. `{str(pk) for pk in db_pks}`) before computing the difference. A raw `set(input_pks) - set(db_pks)` with mixed str/int types will mark all inputs as missing.

item.title: Fetch pk/type pairs once to validate existence and type together
item.description: A single values_list('pk','type') query can serve both the missing-pk check and the wrong-type check, keeping query count flat.
item.content: Instead of separate filter/exclude queries for existence and type validation, fetch `dict(Attribute.objects.filter(pk__in=pks).values_list('pk','type'))` once, derive missing pks from the dict keys and invalid-type pks from its values. This avoids extra queries and keeps error reporting consistent.

item.title: Validate FK targets explicitly before .add() to avoid IntegrityError 500s
item.description: Filter-based validation silently drops nonexistent pks, letting them reach FK constraints and surface as HTTP 500.
item.content: When assigning related objects via `.add()` or similar, explicitly check that all referenced pks exist and return a NOT_FOUND validation error for the missing ones. Filters like `filter(pk__in=...)` silently ignore absent pks, so relying on them alone lets stale client IDs crash on the DB constraint.

item.title: Force evaluation of select_for_update querysets
item.description: Lazy querysets assigned but never evaluated take no FOR UPDATE lock, silently leaving writes unprotected.
item.content: Inside transaction.atomic(), wrap lock querysets in list(...) (e.g. list(qs.values_list('pk', flat=True))) before the bulk_update/write. An unevaluated queryset runs no SQL, so no lock is acquired and the write proceeds unlocked in arbitrary row order, risking deadlocks.

item.title: Use pk-only ordering for lock querysets
item.description: Reviewers rejected ordering locks by mutable fields like sort_order; all lockers should consistently order by pk.
item.content: Lock querysets should order_by('pk') only. Ordering by a mutable field (e.g. sort_order) is not a stable sequence to rely on for lock ordering; streamline new lockers with the existing pk-based ones unless there's a documented reason.

item.title: Add a fixture asserting locks precede writes
item.description: A test fixture that captures queries and asserts an ordered FOR UPDATE runs before the UPDATE catches missing locks.
item.content: Use the assert_locks_rows_before_write fixture (saleor/tests/fixtures.py) in tests around locking code: it captures the block's queries and asserts an ordered FOR UPDATE query is emitted before the UPDATE, catching silently-missing locks.

item.title: Deprecate enum values and subscription types, not just mutations
item.description: When a feature is deprecated, its webhook event enum values and subscription types must also be marked deprecated, not only the mutations.
item.content: For full deprecation, add `deprecation_reason` to the `graphene.Field` declarations of subscription types (e.g. ProductExportCompleted) and to the enum values in WebhookEventTypeEnum, WebhookEventTypeAsyncEnum, and WebhookSampleEventTypeEnum. Reviewers explicitly flagged missing `deprecation_reason` on the three export subscription fields.

item.title: Reuse existing deprecation reason constants
item.description: Define a shared constant for the deprecation message and apply it consistently across all deprecated fields and enum values.
item.content: Add a constant like DEPRECATED_EXPORT_MUTATIONS_TYPE_DESCRIPTION in descriptions.py derived from the existing DEPRECATED_EXPORT_MUTATIONS string, then pass it as `deprecation_reason` to every affected field/enum so the schema output stays consistent.

item.title: Regenerate schema.graphql and update CHANGELOG
item.description: After adding deprecation_reason, regenerate the schema so @deprecated directives appear, and document the change in CHANGELOG.
item.content: Run the schema generation to update saleor/graphql/schema.graphql with `@deprecated(reason: ...)` on each affected enum value. Also add a CHANGELOG entry listing the deprecated event types and subscription types so the change is discoverable.

item.title: Deprecating GraphQL fields via description markers
item.description: Saleor's schema printer converts specific description markers into @deprecated directives, so deprecation must be encoded in descriptions rather than Python-level flags.
item.content: For input fields and arguments, embed the DEPRECATED_IN_3X_INPUT marker verbatim in help_text so schema_printer.print_input_value emits a real @deprecated directive. For types (which have no @deprecated directive), use a plain 'DEPRECATED: ...' prefix in the type description, and never include the DEPRECATED_IN_3X_INPUT marker there because print_description truncates at that marker and would drop the reason.

item.title: Deprecate enum values with a deprecation_reason callable
item.description: graphene.Enum.from_enum accepts a deprecation_reason callable that returns a reason per enum member, enabling selective deprecation of individual error codes.
item.content: Pass deprecation_reason=fn to graphene.Enum.from_enum where fn(enum_member) returns the deprecation text for members to deprecate and None otherwise. This deprecates a single error code (e.g. PREORDER_VARIANT_CANNOT_BE_DEACTIVATED) without touching the rest of the enum.

item.title: Enumerate every surface when deprecating a feature
item.description: A feature deprecation spans mutations, types, input fields, filters, and error codes; missing any surface leaves the API inconsistent.
item.content: Systematically cover: mutations, object types and their fields, input types and their fields, filter fields on all filter inputs (including Where inputs), and enum error codes. Document the full list in CHANGELOG with a migration suggestion (e.g. use regular stock instead of preorder) so users know the replacement path.

item.title: Deprecate all flags in the same category, not just the named ones
item.description: The first attempt was rejected because it deprecated only the storefront flags while leaving `filterableInDashboard` untouched, even though it belongs to the same 'Saleor doesn't tell the UI what to show' category.
item.content: When a deprecation PR targets a category of fields (e.g. presentation flags), scan for all sibling fields in that category and deprecate them together. If a reviewer asks 'should X join this set?', the answer is usually yes—include it and clean up the related input types.

item.title: Centralize deprecation reason strings in descriptions.py
item.description: Define reusable constants like `STOREFRONT_FLAG_DEPRECATION_REASON` and `DASHBOARD_FLAG_DEPRECATION_REASON` in the module's descriptions file and reuse them across filters, inputs, and types.
item.content: Put deprecation reason text in `descriptions.py` as module-level constants so every field (filter, where-filter, mutation input, output type) references the same string. This keeps wording consistent and makes future removal easy to grep.

item.title: Deprecate filters by moving them out of Meta.fields and re-declaring with help_text
item.description: To add deprecation help text to django-filter fields, remove them from `Meta.fields` and declare them explicitly with `help_text` including `DEPRECATED_IN_3X_INPUT` plus the reason.
item.content: For `django_filters.BooleanFilter` fields that need deprecation notices, delete them from `Meta.fields` and re-declare them on the class with `help_text=f"{description}{DEPRECATED_IN_3X_INPUT} {REASON}"`. Apply the same pattern to `BooleanWhereFilter` in the `Where` input.

item.title: Name parameters after their actual type, not a guessed subtype
item.description: A reviewer rejected a parameter named `checkout_user_id` because the function is called with `source_object: Checkout | Order`; renaming to reflect the real source avoids confusion.
item.content: When a helper receives a union-typed object (e.g. `Checkout | Order`), derive the parameter name from the declared type (e.g. `source_object`) or from the extracted value's true meaning (`user_id`), not from one concrete subtype. Reviewers flag misleading names even when behavior is correct.

item.title: Update user-facing docs alongside behavior changes
item.description: The first attempt was rejected partly for not updating the gift-card payment docs; the final diff updated CHANGELOG and docs.
item.content: When changing externally visible behavior (validation rules, error semantics, new restrictions), update the relevant documentation page and CHANGELOG entry in the same change. Reviewers treat missing docs as a blocking issue, not a nit.

item.title: Return generic errors for restricted resources to avoid information leaks
item.description: Restricted gift cards return the same 'code is not valid' message as nonexistent cards, and restriction is checked before balance so balance isn't leaked.
item.content: For access-controlled resources, return an identical generic error for 'not found' and 'not authorized' cases, and order validation checks so that unauthorized callers cannot infer sensitive state (e.g. balance) from error messages. Log the real reason server-side instead.

item.title: Widen URL columns with a shared max-length constant
item.description: When raising a URL field limit, define a single module-level constant matching Django's URLValidator.max_length (2048) and reuse it across all affected models.
item.content: Django's URLValidator caps URLs at 2048 chars, so use that as the canonical limit. Define URL_MAX_LENGTH = 2048 once and apply it to every URL field being widened, keeping model and migration in sync.

item.title: PostgreSQL varchar widening is a cheap migration
item.description: Increasing a varchar length limit in PostgreSQL >= 9.2 is catalog-only, so no table rewrite is needed.
item.content: AlterField that only increases max_length on a CharField/URLField does not rewrite the table in PostgreSQL; the ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock is momentary. Note this in the migration docstring to reassure reviewers.

item.title: Add boundary tests for the new limit
item.description: When changing a field's max_length, add a test that exercises a value exactly at the new limit to prove it is accepted end-to-end.
item.content: Construct a URL of exactly URL_MAX_LENGTH characters (e.g. prefix + padding) and assert the mutation succeeds and persists the value. This guards against regressions and documents the intended boundary.

item.title: Resolve configurable import paths at startup, not lazily
item.description: Reviewers rejected lazy import_string resolution of a settings-provided callable because typos surface only mid-mutation; the codebase already validates such settings in AppConfig.ready().
item.content: When a setting holds a dotted import path, resolve/validate it in AppConfig.ready() (like validate_jwt_manager) so misconfiguration fails at startup. Keep the lazy resolver only as the runtime accessor.

item.title: Refresh MPTT instances after acquiring the tree lock
item.description: Holding an advisory lock is insufficient when the write's math uses in-memory values read before the lock; mptt computes moves from stale instance fields.
item.content: After taking the lock, re-read or call _mptt_refresh() on the nodes involved (e.g. the new parent) so lft/rght/tree_id reflect committed state. Prefer mptt's own refresh over hardcoded field tuples for future-proofing.

item.title: Cover both branches of rebuild logic in tests
item.description: Reviewers flagged that tests only exercised the partial_rebuild path, leaving needs_full_rebuild untested.
item.content: When a repair/rebuild function branches between partial and full rebuild, add a test that forces the full-rebuild condition (e.g. corrupted tree_id or missing interval data) so both paths run.

item.title: Pin exact version when upgrading a dependency
item.description: For dependency upgrade tasks, replace the range specifier with an exact `==<version>` pin in pyproject.toml rather than widening or shifting the range.
item.content: When the issue says 'upgrade X to version Y', set the dependency to `X==Y` (keeping extras like `[standard]`). This makes the intent unambiguous and avoids accidentally resolving to a different version.

item.title: Regenerate uv.lock after editing pyproject.toml
item.description: After changing a dependency version, run `uv lock` so uv.lock reflects the new package and its transitive deps (e.g. httptools) with correct hashes and URLs.
item.content: Dependency upgrades in uv-managed repos require updating both pyproject.toml and uv.lock. The lockfile must include the new version's sdist/wheels and any bumped transitive dependencies; never hand-edit hashes—regenerate via the lock command.

item.title: Respect exclude-newer when choosing upgrade target
item.description: When newer versions exist but are excluded by `exclude-newer`, pick the highest version allowed by that constraint rather than the absolute latest.
item.content: Check the `exclude-newer` setting in pyproject.toml/uv config before selecting a target version. The issue's stated version is usually the newest one permitted by that cutoff; don't try to jump to a version released after the cutoff.

item.title: Verify deprecation-removal scope against domain-layer dependencies
item.description: When removing a deprecated GraphQL API surface, reviewers may flag behavior that depends on fields you removed but that the issue explicitly says to keep.
item.content: Before deleting a field, grep for its consumers in the domain layer (celery tasks, guards, calculations). If the issue says the domain layer stays, keep the DB columns and the code reading them, and state in the changelog that existing data keeps working. Answer reviewer questions about edge cases (e.g. null end dates) by pointing to the unchanged domain behavior rather than re-adding API.

item.title: Remove deprecation helpers together with the deprecated API
item.description: Deprecation description constants and deprecation_reason callbacks become dead code once the deprecated fields are gone.
item.content: When deleting a deprecated type/input/error code, also delete the DEPRECATED_* description constants and any deprecation_reason callable (e.g. product_error_code_deprecation_reason) that referenced it, and drop the deprecation_reason kwarg from the enum factory. Leaving them causes lint failures and confuses future readers.

item.title: Sweep all input/filter/enum locations for a removed field
item.description: A deprecated field typically appears in many inputs, filters and enums; missing one leaves a broken schema or dangling resolver.
item.content: Enumerate every occurrence before editing: create/update/bulk inputs, channel-listing inputs, filter inputs (including WhereInput variants), error-code enums, and resolvers. Then grep the codebase for the field name and its DB column (e.g. is_preorder, preorder_global_threshold, preorder_end_date, preorder_quantity_threshold) to catch cleaning/save paths that must be removed too.

item.title: Enforce pixel limits via Pillow's MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS at app startup
item.description: Setting Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS in AppConfig.ready() covers every decode site, but Pillow only raises above twice the value, so halve the configured limit.
item.content: Pillow warns above Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS and raises DecompressionBombError only above 2x that value. To make your configured limit the actually-enforced one, assign Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS = settings.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS // 2 in AppConfig.ready(). Since it's set once at startup, tests must monkeypatch PIL.Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS directly rather than using the settings fixture.

item.title: Log original exception details, expose sanitized messages to users
item.description: When catching a library exception, preserve its message in logs (with context like filename) but never leak it to API users.
item.content: Reviewers expect the original exception message (e.g. Pillow's pixel count) to be logged with extra context such as the filename, while the user-facing ValidationError uses a clean message referencing settings.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS. Use sanitize_url_for_logging() for any URL fields and consider whether URLs are safe to log at all.

item.title: Add mutation-level regression tests for user-facing validation errors
item.description: Unit tests on validators alone are insufficient; reviewers want end-to-end tests proving the GraphQL mutation returns the expected error code and message.
item.content: When a change alters upload/validation behavior, add a mutation-level test (e.g. productMediaCreate with an oversized image) asserting the error code (FILE_SIZE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED) and readable message, in addition to the validator unit test.

item.title: Cover every entity type the shared code path affects
item.description: When a fix lives in shared attribute-assignment logic, reviewers expect tests for all entity types it touches, not just the ones you happened to write.
item.content: The cleanup applied to products, variants, customers, and pages, but the first attempt only tested product/variant/customer. A reviewer flagged the missing pageUpdate case. Enumerate all callers of the changed code path and add a replace/clear test for each entity type.

item.title: Check webhook/event symmetry when deleting rows implicitly
item.description: Implicitly deleting rows in an update mutation can diverge from the explicit delete mutation's side effects (webhooks, events), which reviewers will call out.
item.content: The explicit attributeValueDelete fires ATTRIBUTE_VALUE_DELETED and ATTRIBUTE_UPDATED webhooks, but the update flow never fired ATTRIBUTE_VALUE_CREATED. Before shipping implicit deletion, verify whether webhook/event emission should match the delete mutation and document or implement the intended behavior.

item.title: Test that sibling/unrelated values survive cleanup
item.description: When deleting detached values, assert that other AttributeValues of the same attribute (unassigned siblings) are not deleted.
item.content: Include an assertion that an unassigned sibling value of the same file attribute still exists after the update, guarding against over-broad deletion queries.

item.title: Distinguish retryable transport errors from permanent validation errors
item.description: When a task has autoretry_for=(IOError,) and a throws= list that skips retries, classify errors by whether retrying could help.
item.content: Malformed headers, 5xx responses, and proxy defects are transient and should raise an IOError subclass (e.g. HTTPError) so autoretry picks them up. Only genuinely permanent conditions (bad content type, oversized file) should raise ValueError to signal give-up. Never let a garbage header destroy persisted data on the first attempt.

item.title: Validate numeric header values for sign and range, not just parseability
item.description: int() accepts negative values, so a -1 Content-Length slips past both the parse try/except and the > max_file_size check.
item.content: After parsing a numeric header, explicitly reject values < 0 (or outside the expected domain) before using them in comparisons. Also remember requests joins duplicate headers with ', ', so '100, 100' will fail int() — treat that as a transport error, not a bad payload.

item.title: Test boundary cases where accumulation exactly equals the limit
item.description: Chunked size checks are usually only tested on the failing side; add a case where chunks sum to exactly max_file_size and expect success.
item.content: Parametrize with max_file_size=2 and chunks [b'a', b'b'] to catch off-by-one errors in `tell() + len(chunk) > max_file_size`. Also cover multi-chunk success, not just single-chunk-at-limit, since the accumulation expression is only exercised on failure otherwise.

item.title: Use db_default, not null=True, for staged column removal
item.description: When de-registering a field from the ORM while keeping its column, make the column nullable via db_default rather than null=True.
item.content: For rolling-deploy-safe field removal, use SeparateDatabaseAndState with state RemoveField and database AlterField adding db_default (e.g. db_default=False / db_default=0). This lets the new ORM insert rows without the column while old pods still read non-NULL values through non-nullable GraphQL fields; null=True would break them.

item.title: Reference an explicit follow-up issue for deferred column drops
item.description: A TODO comment alone is insufficient; migration guidelines require a tracked follow-up issue for the eventual column drop.
item.content: When a migration defers dropping columns to a later release, open a follow-up issue and reference its number in the migration docstring alongside the TODO. Reviewers reject migrations that only say 'remove in X.Y' without a tracked issue.

item.title: Tell affected users what to do in CHANGELOG entries
item.description: Changelog entries for removed behavior should include remediation guidance, not just describe the change.
item.content: When a change removes a capability (e.g. default ordering no longer honors storefrontSearchPosition), state what affected users lose and what they should do instead (sort in storefront, use metadata). Also update tests and fixtures that relied on the old behavior.

item.title: Catch IntegrityError to detect concurrent FK deletion
item.description: When a parent row may be deleted concurrently between a read and a child insert, catch IntegrityError and re-check parent existence to distinguish a lost race from a real bug.
item.content: Wrap the child create in try/except IntegrityError; if the parent no longer exists, raise a NOT_FOUND ValidationError, otherwise re-raise. This avoids masking unrelated constraint violations while giving a clean error for the race.

item.title: Use transaction=True for tests that need real FK checks
item.description: Tests simulating concurrent deletes must commit to the database, so mark them with @pytest.mark.django_db(transaction=True) rather than the default wrapping transaction.
item.content: The default pytest-django transaction wraps the test and prevents the insert from hitting the DB, so foreign key violations never fire. Use transaction=True and clean up any created data manually.

item.title: Avoid unnecessary transaction.atomic() blocks
item.description: Reviewers reject wrapping a single operation in transaction.atomic() since it adds no atomicity benefit.
item.content: Only use transaction.atomic() when multiple statements must succeed or fail together. For a single create/update, skip it to keep code simple and avoid reviewer pushback.

item.title: Refresh denormalized status fields when persisting recalculated totals
item.description: When a function recalculates and saves derived totals, any denormalized status columns derived from those totals must be included in update_fields or they go stale forever.
item.content: In process_order_prices(), charge_status and authorize_status are derived from total_gross_amount but were omitted from the save(update_fields=...) list. Always audit which stored fields are functions of the values being recalculated and add them to update_fields; otherwise the stale value never self-heals because no further events trigger recomputation.

item.title: Cover all state transitions with a parametrized unit test
item.description: A single-direction regression test is insufficient; parametrize over every transition the fix can produce.
item.content: For a status-recalculation fix, add a cheap parametrized unit test next to the changed function covering all directions (e.g. OVERCHARGED->FULL, FULL->PARTIAL, FULL->OVERCHARGED) rather than only the reported case. Reviewers explicitly asked for this; it guards against fixing one direction while breaking another.

item.title: Keep the fix PR minimal and defer data repair
item.description: Separate the code fix from repairing already-affected rows, which needs its own careful design.
item.content: When a denormalized field is wrong, fix the computation in a small PR that can be ported down quickly, and leave backfilling existing bad rows to a separate PR. For backfill, prefer a management command that reports first and applies with a --fix flag over a straight data migration, and account for granted refunds when selecting affected orders.

item.title: Address reviewer nit-picks on naming and comments proactively
item.description: The first attempt was rejected partly for a misleading helper name and an unexplained aggregate choice; fixing these in the final version helped acceptance.
item.content: When a helper returns an attribute (not products), name it accordingly (e.g. `numeric_attribute_with_products`). When using an aggregate like `Min`, add a comment explaining why it is correct (e.g. one value per product, so any aggregate works) to preempt the reader's 'why MIN not MAX' question.

item.title: Parametrize pagination tests on direction and cover backward walk
item.description: Reviewers asked for tests covering both ASC/DESC and `last`+`before` in addition to `first`+`after`, since NULL placement flips with direction.
item.content: For cursor pagination tests, parametrize on sort direction and assert the full order for both forward (`first`+`after`) and backward (`last`+`before`) walks. Also add a representative case for a different attribute type (e.g. dropdown with multiple values) to guard against regressions where the cursor carries `None` in the numeric slot.

item.title: Document breaking cursor changes in CHANGELOG
item.description: The cursor gained a fourth field, invalidating in-flight cursors; reviewers wanted this called out explicitly.
item.content: When a change alters the cursor format (e.g. adding a field), document in the CHANGELOG that cursors issued before the deploy are rejected with 'Received cursor is invalid' and clients must restart from the first page. Also link related long-open issues (e.g. #10125) in the PR description.

item.title: Avoid breaking GraphQL input type renames in released versions
item.description: Renaming an existing GraphQL input type (e.g. TranslationInput to CategoryTranslationInput) breaks all clients and is rejected for already-released minor versions.
item.content: When adding a new mutation that needs a different input shape, introduce a new input type (e.g. ProductMediaTranslationInput) rather than renaming or repurposing an existing shared input type. If a rename is truly needed, target the next major/minor release on main and document the breaking change explicitly.

item.title: Split multi-table migrations and add db_default for zero-downtime
item.description: A single migration touching two tables in one transaction was rejected; new non-null columns need db_default for zero-downtime deploys.
item.content: Create one migration per table change so each runs in its own transaction. For new fields on existing tables, set db_default so the column can be added without a table rewrite and existing rows are populated safely.

item.title: Use description_suffix on TranslationField instead of copy-pasting or per-field ADDED_IN
item.description: Reviewers preferred reusing TranslationField with description_suffix for new translation fields, and ADDED_IN only in Meta.description for new types.
item.content: For a new translation field on an existing type, pass description_suffix=ADDED_IN_3XX to TranslationField rather than duplicating its body. For brand-new types, put ADDED_IN_3XX only in Meta.description and avoid redeclaring fields (like language) already defined by base classes.

item.title: Use add() not set() for M2M relations on shared instances
item.description: Django's set() replaces the entire many-to-many relation, silently detaching rows that other records already linked to the same tag/instance.
item.content: When attaching new objects to an existing shared M2M target (e.g. a tag reused across batches), use `relation.add(*instances)` to insert only missing links. Reserve `set()` for cases where the target's relation should be fully replaced.

item.title: Write regression tests in the reviewer's natural scenario order
item.description: A test that reads existing tags, adds a new one, then creates cards was rejected as 'upside down'; reviewers prefer the plain user flow.
item.content: Structure regression tests as: (1) set up a record with a tag, (2) run the mutation creating new records with another tag, (3) assert the old record kept its tag and the new records have theirs. Avoid convoluted pre-steps that obscure the scenario.

item.title: Check for redundant tests before adding a new one
item.description: Reviewers may point out that an existing test already covers the case, so a new test should add distinct value or be dropped.
item.content: Before adding a regression test, scan existing tests for equivalent coverage; if a parametrized test already exercises the scenario, extend it rather than duplicating. Keep each new test focused on a behavior not otherwise asserted.

item.title: Update version support tables consistently
item.description: When dropping a supported version, update both the supported and unsupported rows in the version table.
item.content: In SECURITY.md the support table has paired rows (e.g. '>= 3.21' supported and '< 3.21' unsupported). Bump both thresholds together so the boundary stays consistent.

item.title: Check EOL dates before choosing the new minimum
item.description: Reviewers may expect the new minimum version to already be past its EOL date.
item.content: Before setting the new supported minimum, verify the release's end-of-life date. If the next version is already EOL (e.g. 3.22 EOL at 6.10), reviewers will flag it, so pick a version that is still actively supported.

item.title: Keep support docs in sync with policy
item.description: Version support changes are small doc edits but must reflect the actual support policy.
item.content: When an issue says a version is no longer supported, update the support matrix to the recommended upgrade target rather than just removing the old row, ensuring the table still covers all versions.

item.title: Replace path filters with in-job change detection for required checks
item.description: GitHub path filters skip the whole workflow, so no check run is reported and required status checks deadlock; move the filter into a job step instead.
item.content: When a workflow must be a required status check, never use `on.pull_request.paths` — a skipped workflow reports nothing. Instead let the job always run, add a first step that diffs changed files against the PR base SHA, and gate subsequent steps with `if: steps.changes.outputs.changed == 'true'`. Treat non-PR events (push, schedule) as `changed=true` so scheduled runs still execute.

item.title: Extract reusable change-detection logic into a composite action
item.description: Reviewers prefer a shared `.github/actions/<name>/action.yml` over duplicated inline shell in each workflow.
item.content: Put the diff-and-match logic in a composite action with a single `additional-file-patterns` input (newline-separated regexes) so each workflow only supplies its own file pattern, e.g. `^\.github/workflows/e2e\.yml$`. Keep the common patterns (`.py`, Dockerfile, source dir, lockfiles) hardcoded inside the action.

item.title: Place step `if` conditions at the top and fail loudly on git errors
item.description: Put `if:` before `run:`/`uses:` for readability, and assign command output to a variable before matching so failures aren't misread as 'no changes'.
item.content: Reviewers flag `if:` placed after `run:` as hard to read — always put it first. In the detection script, capture `changed_files=$(git diff ...)` before grepping so a git failure fails the step rather than yielding an empty match; also fetch the base SHA (`git fetch --depth=1 origin $BASE`) since checkouts are shallow, and drop blank lines from user-supplied patterns because an empty regex matches everything.

item.title: Normalize manifest values explicitly when the validated schema is discarded
item.description: When a manifest validation function validates against a pydantic schema but returns the raw dict, schema-level normalization never reaches downstream code.
item.content: If `clean_manifest_data` validates but discards the `ManifestSchema` instance, any field normalization defined in the schema is lost. Apply the same normalization explicitly at the consumption site (e.g. `install_app`, `AppFetchManifest`) via a shared helper, and add tests for both paths.

item.title: Avoid dead pydantic validators whose return value is unused
item.description: A `field_validator` whose output is discarded adds no behavior and misleads readers about guarantees.
item.content: Before adding a `field_validator`, check whether the validated model instance is actually used. If the caller discards it, remove the validator and do normalization in an explicit function instead; also avoid comments like 'never rejects' when pydantic type checks still run first.

item.title: Reuse existing truncation helpers and naming conventions
item.description: Reviewers expect consistency with existing utilities and test naming in the codebase.
item.content: For length-limited text fields, prefer `django.utils.text.Truncator` (already used for the same 2048 limit in `AppProblem.set_message`) over hand-rolled slicing, and name tests with the established `too_long` phrasing rather than `over_long`.

item.title: Guard default-creating migrations with POPULATE_DEFAULTS
item.description: Data migrations that create default rows must check settings.POPULATE_DEFAULTS and return early when defaults are disabled.
item.content: Add `if not settings.POPULATE_DEFAULTS: return` at the top of any migration that creates default objects, matching existing 'create default' migrations. This prevents duplicate-key loops on logical replicas where defaults are intentionally not populated.

item.title: Make post-migrate tasks tolerate missing defaults
item.description: Celery tasks that look up a default object should catch the domain exception and skip instead of raising.
item.content: When a migration may legitimately not create a default (e.g. POPULATE_DEFAULTS=False), wrap the getter in try/except for its specific exception (NoDefaultCustomerType) and log-and-return. Update tests to assert the skip behavior rather than expecting a raise.

item.title: Explain failure mechanisms concretely in PR descriptions
item.description: Reviewers reject vague failure claims; describe the exact code path and why get_or_create still fails.
item.content: When claiming a bug, trace the actual mechanism (e.g. replica copy of the table racing with the migration's insert, or get_or_create's create branch hitting a duplicate) rather than asserting a symptom. If get_or_create seems safe, verify whether the failure is in the replica copy step, not the migration itself.
